# Problem Statement

In T20 cricket a simple run-rate projection (`current run rate × 20`) ignores *how* the
runs and wickets were produced. Two innings that are both 80/2 after 10 overs can end
at 150 or 190 depending on the batting depth, the recent momentum and — most importantly —
whether a **collapse** is under way. This case study builds two data-science models from
official ball-by-ball IPL data:

1. **Score forecaster (regression)** — expected final first-innings score at 6, 10, 15 and 18 overs.
2. **Collapse detector (classification)** — probability that the batting side loses
   **3 or more wickets in the next 12 legal balls**, using the runs and wickets of the **last 12 balls**
   together with the match state.

# Dataset

* **Source:** Cricsheet — official/licensed ball-by-ball JSON, one file per match (<https://cricsheet.org/>).
* **Size:** 1,169 IPL matches (≈ 2,300 innings, ≈ 280,000 deliveries).
* **Structure:** `info` (teams, venue, season, overs) → `innings` → `overs` → `deliveries`
  (`runs.batter`, `runs.extras`, `runs.total`, `extras.wides/noballs`, `wickets[]`).

Place the JSON files (or the unzipped `ipl_json` folder) in `data/` before knitting.

# Data Parsing & Cleaning

Each JSON file is flattened to **one row per legal ball**. Rules applied:

* only innings 1 and 2 of **20-over** matches (super overs and rain-shortened games removed);
* wides / no-balls are folded into the legal ball they precede, so the ball counter is correct;
* *retired hurt* is **not** a wicket;
* for every legal ball we store score, wickets, **runs and wickets in the last 12 balls**, and
  **wickets in the next 12 balls** (the collapse label).

```{r parse}
ipl <- parse_all_matches(params$data_dir)
cat("Matches :", n_distinct(ipl$match_id), "\n")
cat("Innings :", nrow(distinct(ipl, match_id, innings_num)), "\n")
cat("Rows    :", nrow(ipl), "(one per legal ball)\n")
glimpse(ipl)
```

```{r quality}
# basic data-quality checks
stopifnot(!anyNA(ipl$cum_score), !anyNA(ipl$cum_wickets))
ipl %>% distinct(match_id, innings_num, final_score, final_wickets) %>%
  summarise(min_score = min(final_score), max_score = max(final_score),
            max_wkts = max(final_wickets)) %>% kable()
```

# Exploratory Data Analysis

```{r eda-scores}
innings <- ipl %>% distinct(match_id, innings_num, final_score, final_wickets)
p1 <- ggplot(filter(innings, innings_num == 1), aes(final_score)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, fill = pal["green"], colour = "white") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of first-innings totals",
       x = "Final score", y = "Innings")
print(p1); save_fig(p1, "fig1_score_distribution.png")
```

```{r eda-wickets}
innings %>% filter(innings_num == 1) %>%
  group_by(final_wickets) %>% summarise(innings = n(), mean_score = round(mean(final_score), 1)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Mean first-innings total by wickets lost")
```

# Feature Engineering

| Feature | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `checkpoint_overs` | 6, 10, 15 or 18 overs completed |
| `cum_score`, `cum_wickets` | score and wickets at the checkpoint |
| `current_run_rate` | `cum_score / overs` |
| `runs_last12` | runs scored in the last 12 legal balls (momentum) |
| `wkts_last12` | wickets lost in the last 12 legal balls (pressure) |

```{r snapshots}
snapshots <- ipl %>%
  filter(innings_num == 1, ball %in% CHECKPOINT_BALLS) %>%
  transmute(match_id, checkpoint_overs = ball / 6, cum_score, cum_wickets,
            current_run_rate, runs_last12, wkts_last12, target = final_score)
cat("Checkpoint snapshots:", nrow(snapshots), "\n")
```

# Train / Test Split

The split is made **by match** (80 / 20) so that no match appears in both sets — this avoids
leakage between the same innings' checkpoints.

```{r split}
set.seed(params$seed)
all_ids   <- unique(ipl$match_id)
train_ids <- sample(all_ids, floor(0.8 * length(all_ids)))
train <- filter(snapshots, match_id %in% train_ids)
test  <- filter(snapshots, !match_id %in% train_ids)
cat("Train snapshots:", nrow(train), "| Test snapshots:", nrow(test), "\n")
```

# Model 1 — Score Forecasting

Five approaches are compared: a **mean baseline**, the **naive run-rate projection**
(`CRR × 20`), **linear regression**, **ridge regression**, **random forest** and
**gradient boosting**.

```{r reg-models}
feats <- c("checkpoint_overs", "cum_score", "cum_wickets",
           "current_run_rate", "runs_last12", "wkts_last12")
fml <- as.formula(paste("target ~", paste(feats, collapse = " + ")))

base_val <- mean(train$target)
lm_fit   <- lm(fml, data = train)
ridge_cv <- cv.glmnet(as.matrix(train[, feats]), train$target, alpha = 0)
set.seed(params$seed)
rf_fit   <- randomForest(fml, data = train, ntree = 300, importance = TRUE)
set.seed(params$seed)
gbm_fit  <- gbm(fml, data = train, distribution = "gaussian", n.trees = 800,
                interaction.depth = 3, shrinkage = 0.03, cv.folds = 5, verbose = FALSE)
best_trees <- gbm.perf(gbm_fit, method = "cv", plot.it = FALSE)

preds <- list(
  Baseline        = rep(base_val, nrow(test)),
  `Run-rate x 20` = test$current_run_rate * 20,
  Linear          = as.numeric(predict(lm_fit, test)),
  Ridge           = as.numeric(predict(ridge_cv, as.matrix(test[, feats]), s = "lambda.min")),
  RandomForest    = as.numeric(predict(rf_fit, test)),
  GradientBoost   = as.numeric(predict(gbm_fit, test, n.trees = best_trees))
)
reg_tbl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(preds, function(p) eval_metrics(test$target, p)))
reg_tbl <- data.frame(Model = rownames(reg_tbl), round(reg_tbl, 3), row.names = NULL)
kable(reg_tbl, caption = "Hold-out performance of final-score forecasts (all checkpoints)")
```

```{r reg-by-checkpoint}
best_name <- reg_tbl$Model[which.min(reg_tbl$MAE)]
cat("Best model by MAE:", best_name, "\n")

by_cp <- bind_rows(lapply(c("Run-rate x 20", best_name), function(nm) {
  test %>% mutate(pred = preds[[nm]], model = nm) %>%
    group_by(model, checkpoint_overs) %>%
    summarise(MAE = mean(abs(target - pred)), .groups = "drop")
}))
p3 <- ggplot(by_cp, aes(factor(checkpoint_overs), MAE, fill = model)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(pal["grey"], pal["green"]) %>% setNames(c("Run-rate x 20", best_name))) +
  labs(title = "Forecast error shrinks as the innings unfolds",
       x = "Overs completed", y = "MAE (runs)", fill = NULL)
print(p3); save_fig(p3, "fig3_mae_by_checkpoint.png")
```

```{r pred-actual}
p2 <- test %>% mutate(pred = preds[[best_name]]) %>%
  ggplot(aes(pred, target, colour = factor(checkpoint_overs))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45) + geom_abline(colour = pal["red"], linetype = 2) +
  labs(title = paste("Predicted vs actual final score —", best_name),
       x = "Predicted", y = "Actual", colour = "Overs")
print(p2); save_fig(p2, "fig2_pred_vs_actual.png")
```

## What drives the forecast?

```{r importance}
imp <- as.data.frame(importance(rf_fit))
imp$feature <- rownames(imp)
p4 <- ggplot(imp, aes(reorder(feature, `%IncMSE`), `%IncMSE`)) +
  geom_col(fill = pal["green"]) + coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Random-forest feature importance", x = NULL, y = "% increase in MSE if permuted")
print(p4); save_fig(p4, "fig4_feature_importance.png")
```

# Model 2 — Batting-Collapse Detection

**Definition:** a collapse starts at ball *b* if the batting side loses **≥ 3 wickets in the next 12 legal balls**.
For every legal ball we know the *last-12-ball* runs and wickets (the model inputs) and the
*next-12-ball* wickets (the label). Windows that run past an all-out innings are padded with
"no more wickets"; windows cut short by a successful chase are dropped.

```{r collapse-data}
col_df <- ipl %>% filter(!is.na(is_collapse), ball >= 12)
col_train <- filter(col_df, match_id %in% train_ids)
col_test  <- filter(col_df, !match_id %in% train_ids)
cat("Collapse base rate (test):", round(mean(col_test$is_collapse) * 100, 1), "%\n")

cf <- is_collapse ~ ball + cum_score + cum_wickets + current_run_rate +
  runs_last12 + wkts_last12 + innings_num
```

```{r collapse-models}
lr_fit <- glm(cf, data = col_train, family = binomial)

set.seed(params$seed)
rf_sample <- col_train[sample(nrow(col_train), min(60000, nrow(col_train))), ]
rf_cls <- randomForest(update(cf, factor(is_collapse) ~ .), data = rf_sample,
                       ntree = 150, nodesize = 50)

p_lr_tr <- predict(lr_fit, col_train, type = "response")
p_lr    <- predict(lr_fit, col_test,  type = "response")
p_rf_tr <- predict(rf_cls, col_train[1:min(60000, nrow(col_train)), ], type = "prob")[, 2]
p_rf    <- predict(rf_cls, col_test, type = "prob")[, 2]

thr_lr <- best_f1_threshold(col_train$is_collapse, p_lr_tr)
thr_rf <- best_f1_threshold(col_train$is_collapse[1:length(p_rf_tr)], p_rf_tr)

auc_lr <- as.numeric(auc(roc(col_test$is_collapse, p_lr, quiet = TRUE)))
auc_rf <- as.numeric(auc(roc(col_test$is_collapse, p_rf, quiet = TRUE)))
cm_lr  <- class_metrics(col_test$is_collapse, p_lr, thr_lr)
cm_rf  <- class_metrics(col_test$is_collapse, p_rf, thr_rf)

cls_tbl <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Logistic regression", "Random forest"),
  AUC = round(c(auc_lr, auc_rf), 3),
  Threshold = c(thr_lr, thr_rf),
  Precision = round(c(cm_lr$precision, cm_rf$precision), 3),
  Recall = round(c(cm_lr$recall, cm_rf$recall), 3),
  F1 = round(c(cm_lr$f1, cm_rf$f1), 3),
  Accuracy = round(c(cm_lr$accuracy, cm_rf$accuracy), 3))
kable(cls_tbl, caption = "Collapse detection on the hold-out matches (threshold tuned for F1 on training data)")
```

```{r roc}
roc_df <- bind_rows(
  { r <- roc(col_test$is_collapse, p_lr, quiet = TRUE); data.frame(fpr = 1 - r$specificities, tpr = r$sensitivities, model = "Logistic") },
  { r <- roc(col_test$is_collapse, p_rf, quiet = TRUE); data.frame(fpr = 1 - r$specificities, tpr = r$sensitivities, model = "Random forest") })
p5 <- ggplot(roc_df, aes(fpr, tpr, colour = model)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = pal["grey"]) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Logistic = pal[["red"]], `Random forest` = pal[["green"]])) +
  labs(title = "ROC curves — collapse detection", x = "False-positive rate", y = "True-positive rate", colour = NULL)
print(p5); save_fig(p5, "fig5_roc.png")
```

```{r collapse-heat}
heat <- col_df %>%
  mutate(over_band = cut(ball / 6, c(0, 6, 10, 15, 20), labels = c("1-6", "7-10", "11-15", "16-20")),
         wk_band = pmin(cum_wickets, 7)) %>%
  group_by(over_band, wk_band) %>%
  summarise(rate = mean(is_collapse), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>% filter(n >= 200)
p6 <- ggplot(heat, aes(over_band, factor(wk_band), fill = rate)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(rate, accuracy = 1)), colour = "white", size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = pal["green"], high = pal["red"], labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "How often does a collapse follow?", x = "Overs", y = "Wickets down (7 = 7+)", fill = "Collapse rate")
print(p6); save_fig(p6, "fig6_collapse_heatmap.png")
```

# Live Match Simulator

```{r simulate}
sim <- function(score, wk, overs, r12, w12) {
  snap <- data.frame(checkpoint_overs = overs, cum_score = score, cum_wickets = wk,
                     current_run_rate = score / overs, runs_last12 = r12, wkts_last12 = w12)
  col <- data.frame(ball = overs * 6, cum_score = score, cum_wickets = wk,
                    current_run_rate = score / overs, runs_last12 = r12,
                    wkts_last12 = w12, innings_num = 1)
  cat(sprintf("%d/%d after %.0f overs | last 12 balls: %d runs, %d wkts\n", score, wk, overs, r12, w12))
  cat("Expected final score :", round(predict(rf_fit, snap)), "\n")
  cat("Collapse probability :", round(100 * predict(lr_fit, col, type = "response"), 1), "%\n")
}
sim(85, 2, 10, 15, 0)
sim(85, 4, 10, 8, 2)
```

```{r save}
saveRDS(lr_fit,  "models/ipl_collapse_log_model.rds")
saveRDS(list(best_trees = best_trees), "models/gbm_meta.rds")

by_cp_all <- test %>% mutate(pred = preds[[best_name]]) %>%
  group_by(checkpoint_overs) %>%
  summarise(MAE = mean(abs(target - pred)), .groups = "drop")
rr_cp <- test %>% mutate(pred = preds[["Run-rate x 20"]]) %>%

metrics <- list(
  n_matches = n_distinct(ipl$match_id),
  n_innings = nrow(innings),
  n_balls   = nrow(ipl),
  n_snapshots = nrow(snapshots),
  best_model = best_name,
  forecast = reg_tbl,
  forecast_by_checkpoint = list(best = by_cp_all, run_rate = rr_cp),
  collapse = list(
    base_rate = mean(col_test$is_collapse),
    logistic = c(list(auc = auc_lr, threshold = thr_lr), cm_lr),
    random_forest = c(list(auc = auc_rf, threshold = thr_rf), cm_rf)),
  top_features = rownames(imp)[order(-imp$`%IncMSE`)][1:3]
)
jsonlite::write_json(metrics, "results/metrics.json", auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE, digits = 4)
cat("Saved models/, figures/ and results/metrics.json\n")
```

# Conclusion

* The learned models use **recent momentum** (`runs_last12`), **recent wickets** (`wkts_last12`) and **wickets in hand**,
  which a plain run-rate × 20 projection ignores; the tables above give the exact error comparison on unseen matches.
* Forecast error falls as more overs are completed; the 6-over forecast is inherently the least certain.
* Collapses are rare events; accuracy alone is misleading, so **AUC, precision, recall and F1** are reported.
* **Limitations:** no pitch/weather/batter-quality features; only first-innings totals are forecast
  (chases end early); a random match split is used rather than a season-wise split.
* **Future work:** add batter/bowler form and venue effects, gradient-boosted classifiers with calibration,
  season-wise validation, and a deployed Shiny dashboard (`R/app.R`).
